rv.q: Paddington The Musical, Savoy Theatre (London) Truly this is a great bear. An Ursa Major, as former BBC astronomer Patrick Moore might have said. Or, as the kids of today might put it, the new Paddington musical is 'bear lit, bro'.
For those wearied by the relentless stream of stage musicals based on popular films or books, Paddington is here to scrape the cynicism from their hearts, and to prove how it can be done properly.
This is the new Mary Poppins: a well-known story imaginatively staged, immaculately performed and utterly winning.
Every detail of this show is exquisite – and I confidently predict that this will be one proudly British export that will go on to conquer the world.
Like a big game hunter, it aims at huge moving targets – and hits them, again and again.
It is irresistible; delicious and guilt-free.
And the production becomes intensely moving by the end.
If the cuddly creation at its heart doesn't make it a hit, I'll eat his hat.
Is this a new classic on a par with Mary Poppins or Matilda?
Those few flaws aside, the bear captures our hearts.

The songs by McFly’s Tom Fletcher are very decent: none are sidesplittingly funny, though there are some nicely droll numbers about London, marmalade and whatnot. Furry, funny and fully-formed, the much-anticipated “Paddington” musical has finally arrived in the West End and it’s alive not only with joy but that vanishingly rare theatrical quality: completely beguiling charm.
Paddington the Musical is undoubtedly a very welcome new addition to the London theatre scene.
The Musical achieves is something far more ambitious: a musical that honours Michael Bond's creation while speaking to contemporary audiences with wit, warmth and sophistication.
It wants you to love it, and it is ultimately impossible to resist.
Paddington is pure theatre magic...I tip my hat to Paddington: the small bear is a big hit.
First of all, the show is sensational.
Paddington The Musical is a delightful, high-energy adventure celebrating the possibility of personal change.

Paddington’s story has been adapted for the stage by Jessica Swale with such care, it feels impossible to imagine any way this could have been done better. All of the heart and warmth you would associate with Paddington are all here in great supply, along with some fresh ideas that feel fitting for the theatre.
Paddington The Musical is the right show at the right time.
How glad I am to be wrong, because this show is simply wonderful.
The result of performance and puppetry is complete suspension of doubt.
It is the perfect family show. It's a winner.

You can barely take your eye off the genial little bear as he draws on comedy (darting around knocking over crockery) and heartstrings (his song The Explorer & The Bear is one of the wonderfully tender moments).

cn.t: Critics warmly embrace this charming adaptation, praising the triumphant bear design and heartfelt staging. While some note its sentimentality, most find it a joyous, magical crowd-pleaser that honors Paddington's legacy with wit and warmth.
